legend: Luis likes to play with permutations. A permutation is an arrangement of integers such that if its length is N%%ZSMJ0%%, then each of its elements is between 1%%ZSMJ1%% and N%%ZSMJ2%%, and no element appears more than once. For example, [1,3,4,2]%%ZSMJ3%% and [1,2]%%ZSMJ4%% are permutations, while [1,3,4]%%ZSMJ5%% and [1,2,4,2]%%ZSMJ6%% are not. In a permutation P%%ZSMJ7%% of length N%%ZSMJ8%%, we denote P[1],P[2],…,P[N]%%ZSMJ9%% as its elements in the order they appear in P%%ZSMJ10%%. For example, for P=[1,3,4,2]%%ZSMJ11%%, we have P[3]=4%%ZSMJ12%%.

Luis is interested in the semi-fixed points of permutations. An integer x%%ZSMJ13%% is a semi-fixed point of a permutation P%%ZSMJ14%% if P[P[x]]=x%%ZSMJ15%%. We denote s(P)%%ZSMJ16%% as the number of semi-fixed points of the permutation P%%ZSMJ17%%. For example, for P=[3,6,1,4,2,5]%%ZSMJ18%%, we have s(P)=3%%ZSMJ19%% since 1%%ZSMJ20%%, 3%%ZSMJ21%%, and 4%%ZSMJ22%% are the semi-fixed points of P%%ZSMJ23%%.

Luis is also interested in the rotations of permutations. Given a permutation P%%ZSMJ24%%, rot(P)%%ZSMJ25%% is the permutation obtained by rotating P%%ZSMJ26%% one position to the left. More generally, rotk(P)%%ZSMJ27%% is the result of rotating the permutation P%%ZSMJ28%% exactly k%%ZSMJ29%% positions to the left. For example, for P=[1,3,4,2]%%ZSMJ30%%, we have rot(P)=[3,4,2,1]%%ZSMJ31%%, rot2(P)=[4,2,1,3]%%ZSMJ32%%, and rot3(P)=[2,1,3,4]%%ZSMJ33%%.

Luis came up with a brilliant idea: to combine semi-fixed points with rotations. Given a permutation P%%ZSMJ34%% of length N%%ZSMJ35%%, Luis wants to calculate s(P)+s(rot(P))+s(rot2(P))+⋯+s(rotN−1(P))%%ZSMJ36%% but he does not know how to do it. Would you help him calculate it?
input: The first line contains an integer N%%ZSMJ37%% (1≤N≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ38%%) indicating the length of the permutation.
The second line contains N%%ZSMJ39%% distinct integers P[1],P[2],…,P[N]%%ZSMJ40%% (1≤P[i]≤N%%ZSMJ41%%), the elements of the permutation P%%ZSMJ42%%.
output: A line with an integer, the result of the calculation that Luis wants to compute.
note: In the first example, P=[1,3,4,2]%%ZSMJ43%% and its rotations are:
P=[1,3,4,2]%%ZSMJ44%%, with 1%%ZSMJ45%% semi-fixed point, which is 1%%ZSMJ46%%.
rot2(P)=[4,2,1,3]%%ZSMJ48%%, with 1%%ZSMJ49%% semi-fixed point, which is 2%%ZSMJ50%%.
rot3(P)=[2,1,3,4]%%ZSMJ51%%, with 4%%ZSMJ52%% semi-fixed points, which are 1,2,3%%ZSMJ53%%, and 4%%ZSMJ54%%.
